title: Roast Masala Mango Haloumi and Potato
subtitle: with 'Onion Bhajis' and Cucumber Pickle
description: Our vegetarian dishes are crammed with vibrant, flavoursome goodness, from the first delicious bite to the very last. Whether you’ve taken the full vegetarian plunge or like mixing things up with a few meat-free nights, you’ll love our exciting, ever-changing vegetarian offerings.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line 2 oven trays with baking paper. Thinly slice the onion. Cut the potato into 1cm-thick slices. Slice the haloumi. Thinly slice the cucumber. Combine 2 tsp white vinegar and 1 tsp sugar in a large bowl. Add the cucumber and toss to coat. Set aside to pickle, tossing occasionally, until needed.

Make onion bhajis: Combine the onion, 1 tsp vegetable oil and 2 tsp plain flour in a bowl (see Make it yours). Put the onion mixture on a lined tray. Bake for 20-25 mins until the onions are crispy on the outside.

Bake potato: Meanwhile, put the potato, half the masala seasoning and 2 tsp vegetable oil in a bowl, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Put the seasoned potatoes on the remaining lined tray and reserve the bowl. Bake for 10-15 mins until just tender.

Bake haloumi: Put the haloumi, mango chutney, remaining masala seasoning and 1 tsp vegetable oil in the reserved bowl. Season with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Spoon the haloumi mixture on top of the potato and cook for a further 10 mins or until the potato is tender.
Serve up: Divide the masala mango mixture and onion bhajis among plates. Drizzle over the yoghurt and top with the pickled cucumber. Enjoy!
Make it yours: Pushed for time? Or not wanting crispy onions. No worries. Simply omit the flour, and add the onions to the tray with the potatoes in Step 3.
